newsitem.title: UK: Hong Kong insurance body to be independent - paper.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong insurance body to be independent - paper.

text.p: The Insurance Commission hopes to become fully independent this year, severing links with the Government for the first time, Insurance Commissioner Alan Wong Chi-kong told a newspaper on Tuesday.

According to the South China Morning Post, he said the decision followed similar moves by the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) in 1989 and the creation of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) in 1993, both of which were previously linked to the Government.
Mr Wong said a report on the proposals would be submitted to the Government in the middle of the year and that he was hopeful the plan would be approved this year.

According to the newspaper, Mr Wong said: "After the split, the office will have more flexibility to decide its own structure and will also have a better image overseas if we are seen to be outside the Government."
